claim: Neurokinin B (NKB) signaling is critical for reproduction in all studied species.
source: Neurokinin B (NKB) signaling is critical for reproduction in all studied species.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific consensus about NKB's role in reproduction.

claim: The existing consensus is that NKB induces GnRH release via kisspeptin (Kiss1) stimulation in the arcuate nucleus.
source: The existing consensus is that NKB induces GnRH release via kisspeptin (Kiss1) stimulation in the arcuate nucleus.
evidence: This statement refers to the established scientific consensus in the field.

claim: The stimulatory action of NKB is dependent on circulating estrogen (E2) levels.
source: However, the stimulatory action of NKB is dependent on circulating estrogen (E2) levels, without which, NKB inhibits luteinizing hormone (LH) release.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations described in the manuscript and references to prior work.

claim: Without estrogen, NKB inhibits luteinizing hormone (LH) release.
source: However, the stimulatory action of NKB is dependent on circulating estrogen (E2) levels, without which, NKB inhibits luteinizing hormone (LH) release.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1A,B showing decreased LH after senktide in the absence of sex steroids.

claim: The evidence supporting the kisspeptin-dependent role of NKB derives from models of persistent hypogonadal state with reduced E2 levels.
source: Importantly, the evidence supporting the kisspeptin-dependent role of NKB, derives from models of persistent hypogonadal state [e.g. Kiss1r knock-out (KO) mice], with reduced E2 levels.
evidence: This is an inference based on analysis of previous studies in the field.

claim: In the presence of E2, NKB signaling induces LH release in a kisspeptin-independent manner through the activation of NK3R neurons in the posterodorsal medial amygdala (MePD).
source: Here, we demonstrate that in the presence of E2, NKB signaling induces LH release in a kisspeptin-independent manner through the activation of NK3R (NKB receptor) neurons in the posterodorsal medial amygdala (MePD).
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Chemogenetic activation of MePD Kiss1 neurons induces LH release.
source: Importantly, we show that chemogenetic activation of MePD Kiss1 neurons induces LH release, however, the stimulatory action of NKB in this area is Kiss1 neuron-independent.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The stimulatory action of NKB in the MePD is Kiss1 neuron-independent.
source: Importantly, we show that chemogenetic activation of MePD Kiss1 neurons induces LH release, however, the stimulatory action of NKB in this area is Kiss1 neuron-independent.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing LH increase after senktide in Kiss1 KO mice (Figure 4D).

claim: Two independent neuronal circuitries within the MePD regulate reproductive function in females.
source: These results document the existence of two independent neuronal circuitries within the MePD that regulate reproductive function in females.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing both Kiss1-dependent and NK3R-dependent pathways in the MePD.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in the genes encoding for kisspeptin (Kiss1) or its receptor (Kiss1r) in humans and mice are linked to hypogonadotropic-hypogonadism and infertility.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in the genes encoding for kisspeptin (Kiss1) or its receptor (Kiss1r) or NKB (encoded by the Tac2 gene) and its receptor (NK3R, encoded by the Tacr3 gene) in humans and mice, are linked to hypogonadotropic-hypogonadism and infertility (Seminara et al., 2003; Topaloglu et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in NKB (encoded by the Tac2 gene) and its receptor (NK3R, encoded by the Tacr3 gene) in humans and mice are linked to hypogonadotropic-hypogonadism and infertility.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in the genes encoding for kisspeptin (Kiss1) or its receptor (Kiss1r) or NKB (encoded by the Tac2 gene) and its receptor (NK3R, encoded by the Tacr3 gene) in humans and mice, are linked to hypogonadotropic-hypogonadism and infertility (Seminara et al., 2003; Topaloglu et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Kisspeptins are secreted from Kiss1 neurons in the arcuate (Kiss1ARC) and anteroventral periventricular/periventricular (Kiss1AVPV/PeN) nuclei.
source: Kisspeptins, secreted from Kiss1 neurons in the arcuate (Kiss1ARC) and anteroventral periventricular/periventricular (Kiss1AVPV/PeN) nuclei, have been directly linked to the release of gonadotropin releasing hormone [GnRH (Smith et al., 2006; Fergani and Navarro, 2016)
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Kisspeptins have been directly linked to the release of gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH).
source: Kisspeptins, secreted from Kiss1 neurons in the arcuate (Kiss1ARC) and anteroventral periventricular/periventricular (Kiss1AVPV/PeN) nuclei, have been directly linked to the release of gonadotropin releasing hormone [GnRH (Smith et al., 2006; Fergani and Navarro, 2016)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous research.

claim: There is a population of Kiss1 neurons in the posterodorsal part of the medial amygdala (Kiss1MePD).
source: however, there is another population of Kiss1 neurons in the posterodorsal part of the medial amygdala (Kiss1MePD) whose contribution to GnRH/LH stimulation has not yet been described (Fergani and Navarro, 2016; Smith et al., 2006; Pineda et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous anatomical studies.

claim: The contribution of Kiss1MePD neurons to GnRH/LH stimulation has not yet been described.
source: however, there is another population of Kiss1 neurons in the posterodorsal part of the medial amygdala (Kiss1MePD) whose contribution to GnRH/LH stimulation has not yet been described (Fergani and Navarro, 2016; Smith et al., 2006; Pineda et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: Kiss1ARC neurons express neurokinin B and dynorphin.
source: In addition to kisspeptin, Kiss1ARC neurons express neurokinin B and dynorphin and these neurons are sometimes referred to as KNDy neurons (Fergani and Navarro, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citation.

claim: Kiss1ARC neurons are sometimes referred to as KNDy neurons.
source: In addition to kisspeptin, Kiss1ARC neurons express neurokinin B and dynorphin and these neurons are sometimes referred to as KNDy neurons (Fergani and Navarro, 2016).
evidence: This is established nomenclature in the field.

claim: The stimulatory effect of NKB/NK3R signaling lies up-stream of Kiss1/Kiss1r, which in turn directly activates GnRH neurons.
source: Functional studies in mice and other species suggest that the stimulatory effect of NKB/NK3R signaling lies up-stream of Kiss1/Kiss1r, which in turn, directly activates GnRH neurons and, hence, stimulates luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) secretion into the peripheral circulation (García-Galiano et al., 2012; Grachev et al., 2012; Navarro et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to functional studies in multiple species.

claim: NKB signaling onto kisspeptin occurs via the auto-synaptic activation of NK3R residing on Kiss1ARC neurons.
source: Specifically, NKB signaling onto kisspeptin occurs via the auto-synaptic activation of NK3R residing on Kiss1ARC neurons (Fergani and Navarro, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The selective NK3R agonist, senktide, induces Fos expression in Kiss1ARC neurons in vivo.
source: The existence of this pathway is supported by the fact that the selective NK3R agonist, senktide, induces Fos expression in Kiss1ARC neurons in vivo (Navarro et al., 2011a)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous experimental work.

claim: Senktide increases the electrical activity of Kiss1ARC neurons in hypothalamic slices.
source: The existence of this pathway is supported by the fact that the selective NK3R agonist, senktide, induces Fos expression in Kiss1ARC neurons in vivo (Navarro et al., 2011a) and increases their electrical activity in hypothalamic slices (de Croft et al., 2013; Navarro et al., 2011b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous electrophysiological studies.

claim: The stimulatory effect of senktide on LH secretion is absent in Kiss1r knock out (KO) mice.
source: Subsequently, kisspeptin signaling was deemed an indispensable part of the reproductive role of NKB, as the stimulatory effect of senktide on LH secretion was shown to be absent in Kiss1r knock out (KO) mice (García-Galiano et al., 2012; Navarro et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The stimulatory effect of senktide on LH secretion is absent in prepubertal rats treated with a Kiss1r antagonist.
source: Subsequently, kisspeptin signaling was deemed an indispensable part of the reproductive role of NKB, as the stimulatory effect of senktide on LH secretion was shown to be absent in Kiss1r knock out (KO) mice (García-Galiano et al., 2012; Navarro et al., 2015), prepubertal rats treated with a Kiss1r antagonist (Grachev et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The stimulatory effect of senktide on LH secretion is absent in agonadal juvenile monkeys with a desensitized Kiss1r.
source: Subsequently, kisspeptin signaling was deemed an indispensable part of the reproductive role of NKB, as the stimulatory effect of senktide on LH secretion was shown to be absent in Kiss1r knock out (KO) mice (García-Galiano et al., 2012; Navarro et al., 2015), prepubertal rats treated with a Kiss1r antagonist (Grachev et al., 2012) or agonadal juvenile monkeys with a desensitized Kiss1r (Ramaswamy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The effect of NK3R activation via ICV administration of senktide on LH release is highly dependent on the sex steroid milieu.
source: Interestingly, the effect of NK3R activation via intracerebroventricular (ICV) administration of senktide on LH release is highly dependent on the sex steroid milieu; senktide was inhibitory in the absence but stimulatory in the presence of sex steroids in mice (Navarro et al., 2015) and sheep (Billings et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies in mice and sheep.

claim: Senktide is inhibitory on LH release in the absence of sex steroids in mice.
source: Interestingly, the effect of NK3R activation via intracerebroventricular (ICV) administration of senktide on LH release is highly dependent on the sex steroid milieu; senktide was inhibitory in the absence but stimulatory in the presence of sex steroids in mice (Navarro et al., 2015) and sheep (Billings et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation and confirmed by data in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Senktide is stimulatory on LH release in the presence of sex steroids in mice.
source: Interestingly, the effect of NK3R activation via intracerebroventricular (ICV) administration of senktide on LH release is highly dependent on the sex steroid milieu; senktide was inhibitory in the absence but stimulatory in the presence of sex steroids in mice (Navarro et al., 2015) and sheep (Billings et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation and confirmed by data in Figure 1C,D.

claim: A subset of GnRH neurons contains NK3R in rats.
source: Furthermore, a subset of GnRH neurons has been shown to contain NK3R in rats (Krajewski et al., 2005) and mice (Navarro et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous anatomical studies.

claim: A subset of GnRH neurons contains NK3R in mice.
source: Furthermore, a subset of GnRH neurons has been shown to contain NK3R in rats (Krajewski et al., 2005) and mice (Navarro et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous anatomical studies.

claim: A kisspeptin-independent activation of GnRH neurons by NK3R agonists in the median eminence has been demonstrated in vitro.
source: and a kisspeptin-independent activation of GnRH neurons, by NK3R agonists, in the median eminence (ME) has been demonstrated in vitro (Gaskins et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous in vitro work.

claim: Homozygous Kiss1cre/cre mice are Kiss1 KO and display severe hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
source: We used mice in which Cre recombinase was targeted to the Kiss1 locus and prevented Kiss1 protein synthesis; consequently, homozygous mice (Kiss1cre/cre) are Kiss1 KO and display severe hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (Padilla et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the characterization of this mouse model.

claim: ICV senktide administration decreased plasma LH levels by ~50% in WT males in the absence of testosterone.
source: In the absence of sex steroids [testosterone (T) or E2, in males and females, respectively)] ICV senktide administration decreased plasma LH levels by ~50% in WT males (p < 0.0001)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ICV senktide administration decreased plasma LH levels by ~36% in WT females in the absence of estradiol.
source: In the absence of sex steroids [testosterone (T) or E2, in males and females, respectively)] ICV senktide administration decreased plasma LH levels by ~50% in WT males (p < 0.0001) and ~36% in WT females (p = 0.0016)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: ICV senktide administration caused no alteration in LH in Kiss1 KO mice of either sex in the absence of sex steroids.
source: In the absence of sex steroids [testosterone (T) or E2, in males and females, respectively)] ICV senktide administration decreased plasma LH levels by ~50% in WT males (p < 0.0001) and ~36% in WT females (p = 0.0016) with no alteration observed in Kiss1 KO mice of either sex (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: When circulating levels of sex steroids were restored, LH release was significantly increased in WT males (p = 0.0049).
source: When circulating levels of sex steroids were restored, LH release was significantly increased in WT males and females [(WTOVX+E2, WTORX+T); p = 0.007 and p = 0.0049, respectively; Figure 1C,D].
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: When circulating levels of sex steroids were restored, LH release was significantly increased in WT females (p = 0.007).
source: When circulating levels of sex steroids were restored, LH release was significantly increased in WT males and females [(WTOVX+E2, WTORX+T); p = 0.007 and p = 0.0049, respectively; Figure 1C,D].
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: LH release was significantly increased in Kiss1 KO female mice supplemented with E2 after senktide administration (p = 0.005).
source: Interestingly, the same was observed in Kiss1 KO female mice supplemented with E2 [(Kiss1 KO+E2); p = 0.005; Figure 1D]
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: LH release was not increased in male Kiss1 KO mice supplemented with T after senktide administration.
source: Interestingly, the same was observed in Kiss1 KO female mice supplemented with E2 [(Kiss1 KO+E2); p = 0.005; Figure 1D] but not in male Kiss1 KO mice supplemented with T (Kiss1 KO+T; Figure 1C)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: There exists a female-specific, kisspeptin-independent but E2-dependent, NKB/NK3R signaling pathway that controls LH release.
source: but not in male Kiss1 KO mice supplemented with T (Kiss1 KO+T; Figure 1C) revealing the existence of a female-specific, kisspeptin-independent but E2-dependent, NKB/NK3R signaling pathway that controls LH release.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing male and female responses.

claim: mCherry expression was present throughout the ARC and not elsewhere after AAV injection.
source: Analysis following the completion of pharmacological studies demonstrated that mCherry expression was present throughout the ARC (Figure 2B) and not elsewhere.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: mCherry spread extended throughout the medial-caudal extent of the ARC (approximately −1.40 mm to −2.30 mm from bregma).
source: There was limited variability in the spread of mCherry among animals which extended throughout the medial-caudal extent of the ARC (approximately −1.40 mm to −2.30 mm from bregma; paxinos atlas).
evidence: This is based on anatomical analysis of injection sites.

claim: Within the ARC, HM3D:mCherry was expressed in ~32% of GFP-immunoreactive cells.
source: Within the ARC, of both Kiss1Cre/+ and Kiss1 KO genotypes, HM3D:mCherry was expressed in ~32% of GFP-immunoreactive cells, and was not observed in non-GFP cells or other brain areas.
evidence: This is based on quantitative immunohistochemical analysis.

claim: HM3D:mCherry was not observed in non-GFP cells or other brain areas after ARC injection.
source: Within the ARC, of both Kiss1Cre/+ and Kiss1 KO genotypes, HM3D:mCherry was expressed in ~32% of GFP-immunoreactive cells, and was not observed in non-GFP cells or other brain areas.
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical analysis confirming specificity of viral infection.

claim: Kiss1Cre/+ animals treated with CNO showed a significant increase in LH within the first 15 min after the injection (p = 0.0057) compared to controls.
source: Kiss1Cre/+ animals treated with clozapine N-oxide (CNO) showed a significant increase in LH within the first 15 min after the injection (p = 0.0057) compared to controls, which was sustained until the end of the sampling period (90 min; p < 0.0001; Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The LH increase in Kiss1Cre/+ animals after CNO was sustained until the end of the sampling period (90 min; p < 0.0001).
source: Kiss1Cre/+ animals treated with clozapine N-oxide (CNO) showed a significant increase in LH within the first 15 min after the injection (p = 0.0057) compared to controls, which was sustained until the end of the sampling period (90 min; p < 0.0001; Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: No effect on LH release was observed in E2-supplemented Kiss1 KO animals treated with either saline or CNO.
source: However, no effect on LH release was observed in E2-supplemented Kiss1 KO (i.e. Kiss1cre/cre) animals treated with either saline or CNO (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Only mice with an intact Kiss1 signaling system showed an increase in LH release after chemogenetic activation of ARC Kiss1 neurons.
source: Therefore, only mice with an intact Kiss1 signaling system showed an increase in LH release, despite similar activation of the Kiss1ARC neuron in both mouse models after CNO treatment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the responses in Kiss1Cre/+ and Kiss1 KO mice.

claim: The stimulation of LH release after senktide in Kiss1 KO animals must occur via a different NK3R-expressing neuronal population than ARC KNDy neurons.
source: Thus, the stimulation of LH release after senktide in Kiss1 KO animals must occur via a different NK3R-expressing neuronal population.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of LH response after ARC Kiss1 neuron activation in Kiss1 KO mice.

claim: Large NK3R immunoreactive neurons and fibers were identified in the substantia innominata, paraventricular nucleus, supraoptic nucleus, lateral hypothalamus, zona incerta, and perifornical regions.
source: Large NK3R immunoreactive neurons and fibers were identified in the substantia innominata, paraventricular nucleus, supraoptic nucleus, lateral hypothalamus, zona incerta, and perifornical regions.
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical analysis of NK3R distribution.

claim: In the ARC, cells containing NK3R were evident only in WTOVX and hypogonadal Kiss1 KO female mice.
source: Interestingly, in the ARC, cells containing NK3R were evident only in WTOVX and hypogonadal Kiss1 KO female mice (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the MePD, NK3R cell bodies appeared only when WT and Kiss1 KO females were supplemented with E2.
source: whereas, in the MePD, NK3R cell bodies appeared only when WT and Kiss1 KO females were supplemented with E2 (Figure 4A, B and C).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4A, B and C.

claim: Minimal close appositions were observed between NK3R and GnRH in the ARC and medial septum.
source: Next, we investigated the anatomical relationship of NK3R and GnRH expression with dual-label immunohistochemistry, which revealed minimal close appositions between the two proteins in the ARC and medial septum (MS) (Figure 3A and C).
evidence: This is based on dual-label immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 3A and C.

claim: GnRH cells and fibers showed intermingling with NK3R containing cells and fibers in the ARC and MS, but no co-expression within GnRH cell bodies.
source: In these two areas, GnRH cells and fibers showed intermingling with NK3R containing cells and fibers, but no co-expression within GnRH cell bodies (>100 cells analyzed from a total of 16 mice; Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of >100 GnRH cells from 16 mice.

claim: No fibers containing NK3R immunoreactivity were observed in the internal or external zone of the median eminence.
source: Interestingly, we observed no fibers containing NK3R immunoreactivity in the internal or external zone of the median eminence (ME; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Senktide administration into the ARC of WTOVX+E2 mice stimulated LH secretion within 15 min from drug infusion (p < 0.0001).
source: Senktide administration into the ARC or POA of WTOVX+E2 mice stimulated LH secretion within 15 min from drug infusion (Figure 3D and E; p < 0.0001 for both) compared to Kiss1 KO animals.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Senktide administration into the POA of WTOVX+E2 mice stimulated LH secretion within 15 min from drug infusion (p < 0.0001).
source: Senktide administration into the ARC or POA of WTOVX+E2 mice stimulated LH secretion within 15 min from drug infusion (Figure 3D and E; p < 0.0001 for both) compared to Kiss1 KO animals.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: When senktide was administered into the MePD of WTOVX+E2 and Kiss1 KO females supplemented with E2, a robust increase in LH was observed within 15 min after senktide infusion that was similar in both genotypes.
source: However, when senktide was administered into the MePD of WTOVX+E2 and Kiss1 KO females supplemented with E2 a robust increase in LH was observed within 15 min after senktide infusion that was similar in both genotypes (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: In the absence of E2, Kiss1 KO females did not show any alteration in LH release after senktide administration into the MePD.
source: Conversely, in the absence of E2, Kiss1 KO females did not show any alteration in LH release (Figure 4D), mimicking the LH responses we obtained after an ICV injection of senktide in these animals (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: HM3Dq:mCherry expression in the MePD was limited to sections ranging from −1.6 mm to −2.0 mm from bregma.
source: HM3Dq:mCherry expression was present in the MePD (Figure 4F) and was limited to sections ranging from (from −1.6 mm to −2.0 mm from bregma; paxinos atlas).
evidence: This is based on anatomical analysis of injection sites.

claim: Within the MePD, mCherry cell bodies were co-expressed in ~89% of GFP-immunoreactive cells.
source: Within the MePD, mCherry cell bodies were co-expressed in ~89% of GFP-immunoreactive cells (i.e. Kiss1 cells), and was not observed in non-GFP cells.
evidence: This is based on quantitative immunohistochemical analysis.

claim: mCherry was not observed in non-GFP cells in the MePD.
source: Within the MePD, mCherry cell bodies were co-expressed in ~89% of GFP-immunoreactive cells (i.e. Kiss1 cells), and was not observed in non-GFP cells.
evidence: This confirms the specificity of viral infection to Kiss1 neurons.

claim: Kiss1Cre/+ mice expressing hM3Dq:mCherry in the MePD and treated with CNO had an increase in LH within 30 min after the injection (p = 0.0107) compared to animals receiving saline treatment.
source: Kiss1Cre/+ mice expressing hM3Dq:mCherry in the MePD and treated with CNO to activate the Kiss1MePD neurons, had an increase in LH within 30 min after the injection (p = 0.0107) compared to animals receiving saline treatment, which was sustained for another 30 min before returning to basal levels (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The LH increase in Kiss1Cre/+ mice after CNO activation of MePD Kiss1 neurons was sustained for another 30 min before returning to basal levels.
source: Kiss1Cre/+ mice expressing hM3Dq:mCherry in the MePD and treated with CNO to activate the Kiss1MePD neurons, had an increase in LH within 30 min after the injection (p = 0.0107) compared to animals receiving saline treatment, which was sustained for another 30 min before returning to basal levels (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: No alteration in LH was observed in E2-supplemented Kiss1 KO animals treated with either saline or CNO after MePD injection.
source: No alteration in LH was observed in E2-supplemented Kiss1 KO animals treated with either saline or CNO (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: The MePD is a component of the gonadotropin axis.
source: Our results provide evidence that the MePD is a component of the gonadotropin axis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing LH responses to MePD manipulations.

claim: Activation of Kiss1MePD neurons stimulates LH release into the peripheral circulation.
source: Specifically, we have identified two independent pathways within the MePD that can lead to the stimulation of GnRH/LH release. The first involves Kiss1MePD neurons, the activation of which, stimulates LH release into the peripheral circulation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: LH stimulation by Kiss1MePD neurons is achieved by the release of kisspeptin and not by any other signaling molecules produced within the Kiss1MePD neuron.
source: Furthermore, this is achieved by the release of kisspeptin and not by any other signaling molecules produced within the Kiss1MePD neuron, since LH was increased only in animals with an intact kisspeptin signaling system.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of LH response in Kiss1 KO mice (Figure 4H).

claim: Kisspeptin is not a required mediator between NK3R activation in the MePD and LH secretion.
source: A second pathway, involving NKB/NK3R signaling, was also identified, when senktide (NK3R agonist) administration into the MePD induced LH release in Kiss1 KO mice (Padilla et al., 2018). Thus, kisspeptin is not a required mediator between NK3R activation in the MePD and LH secretion.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing LH increase after senktide in Kiss1 KO mice (Figure 4D).

claim: The NK3R-mediated LH stimulation pathway in the MePD is female-specific and estrogen-dependent.
source: Interestingly, this pathway is female-specific and estrogen-dependent as responses were absent in males and hypogonadal femalesFigure 1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 comparing males and females with and without sex steroids.

claim: The kisspeptin-independent action of NKB cannot be attributed to direct stimulation of NK3R located on GnRH neurons.
source: Overall, our data suggest that the kisspeptin-independent action of NKB cannot be attributed to direct stimulation of NK3R located on GnRH neurons.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of NK3R-GnRH colocalization and minimal anatomical interactions.

claim: Kiss1ARC (KNDy) neurons make close appositions with GnRH cell bodies and terminals.
source: Kiss1ARC (KNDy) neurons make close appositions with GnRH cell bodies and terminals (Lehman et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous anatomical studies.

claim: Senktide induces GnRH release from the ME in vitro, and this effect is in part present in Kiss1 KO mice.
source: For example, it has been demonstrated with in vitro examination of coronal brain slices, that senktide induces GnRH release from the ME and this effect is, in part, present in Kiss1 KO mice (Gaskins et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous in vitro work.

claim: Activation of the Kiss1ARC (KNDy) neuron stimulated LH release only in mice with an intact kisspeptin signaling system and was completely absent in Kiss1 KO mice.
source: However, activation of the Kiss1ARC (KNDy) neuron stimulated LH release only in mice with an intact kisspeptin signaling system and was completely absent in Kiss1 KO mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Kisspeptin, but no other signaling molecule produced by Kiss1ARC (KNDy) neurons can stimulate LH release in vivo.
source: This provides evidence that kisspeptin, but no other signaling molecule produced by Kiss1ARC (KNDy) neurons can stimulate LH release in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of LH response in Kiss1 KO mice after chemogenetic activation of ARC Kiss1 neurons.

claim: Non-specific clozapine effects are not an issue in the Kiss1Cre mouse model used in this study.
source: However, this does not appear to be the case in the current Kiss1Cre mouse model as Kiss1 KO mice were injected with an identical protocol as heterozygous (Kiss1Cre/+) and yet showed no alteration in LH. Thus, we can conclude that non-specific clozapine effects are not an issue in this model.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential responses between Kiss1Cre/+ and Kiss1 KO mice.

claim: Estrogen downregulated NK3R expression in the ARC.
source: Specifically, estrogen downregulated NK3R expression in the ARC whereas the opposite was true for the MePD, with more NK3R containing cell bodies evident when animals were supplemented with E2.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Estrogen upregulated NK3R expression in the MePD.
source: Specifically, estrogen downregulated NK3R expression in the ARC whereas the opposite was true for the MePD, with more NK3R containing cell bodies evident when animals were supplemented with E2.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4A, B and C.

claim: High sensitivity of NK3R expression to E2 has been reported for the ARC with in situ hybridization studies.
source: High sensitivity of NK3R expression to E2, has also been reported for the ARC with in situ hybridization studies (Navarro et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous studies.

claim: The regulation of NK3R expression by E2 is reminiscent of the regulation of Kiss1 by E2 in the ARC and MePD.
source: Interestingly, this regulation of NK3R expression is reminiscent of the regulation of Kiss1 by E2 in these areas (Kim et al., 2011; Smith et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a comparison to established knowledge about Kiss1 regulation, supported by citations.

claim: LH release as a result of NKB/NK3R signaling in the POA or ARC is predominantly achieved via initial kisspeptin release.
source: Therefore, our data suggest that LH release, as a result of NKB/NK3R signaling in the POA or ARC, is predominantly achieved via initial kisspeptin release, involving Kiss1AVPV/PeN and/or Kiss1ARC neuron activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential responses between WT and Kiss1 KO mice after senktide injection into POA or ARC.

claim: 10% of Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons contain NK3R.
source: Indeed, 10% of Kiss1AVPV/PeN and virtually all Kiss1ARC neurons contain NK3R (Navarro et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous anatomical studies.

claim: Virtually all Kiss1ARC neurons contain NK3R.
source: Indeed, 10% of Kiss1AVPV/PeN and virtually all Kiss1ARC neurons contain NK3R (Navarro et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous anatomical studies.

claim: Kiss1ARC cells project to Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons and GnRH cell bodies and terminals.
source: Moreover, both populations are interconnected, Kiss1ARC cells project to Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons and GnRH cell bodies and terminals (Yip et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous anatomical studies.

claim: NK3R-expressing cells in the MePD do not co-localize with NKB.
source: Furthermore, these NK3R expressing cells do not co-localize with NKB, but are surrounded by a plethora of NKB fibers (Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: NK3R-expressing cells in the MePD are surrounded by a plethora of NKB fibers.
source: Furthermore, these NK3R expressing cells do not co-localize with NKB, but are surrounded by a plethora of NKB fibers (Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Likely sources of NKB fibers in the MePD include NKB-expressing cells residing within the ARC or the neighboring NKB population in the central amygdala (CeA).
source: Likely candidates include NKB-expressing cells residing within the ARC or the neighboring NKB population in the central amygdala (CeA) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) to date, implicated only in the modulation of fear memories (Andero et al., 2016).
evidence: This is speculation about the source of NKB fibers based on anatomical observations.

claim: NKB in the central amygdala has been implicated in the modulation of fear memories.
source: Likely candidates include NKB-expressing cells residing within the ARC or the neighboring NKB population in the central amygdala (CeA) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) to date, implicated only in the modulation of fear memories (Andero et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Chemogenetic activation of the Kiss1MePD neuron provided evidence that the activation of Kiss1 neurons in the MePD of the female mouse can stimulate LH but only through the release of kisspeptin.
source: Chemogenetic activation of the Kiss1MePD neuron provided evidence that the activation of Kiss1 neurons in the MePD of the female mouse can stimulate LH but only through the release of kisspeptin.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential responses between Kiss1Cre/+ and Kiss1 KO mice.

claim: GnRH/LH stimulation via the Kiss1MePD neuron is most likely not part of the kisspeptin-independent NKB/NK3R signaling pathway but of a second LH stimulating mechanism originating from the MePD.
source: Furthermore, GnRH/LH stimulation via the Kiss1MePD neuron is most likely not part of the kisspeptin-independent NKB/NK3R signaling pathway but of a second LH stimulating mechanism originating from the MePD.
evidence: This is inferred from the distinct responses to Kiss1 neuron activation versus NK3R activation in the MePD.

claim: An injection of kisspeptin specifically into the amygdala results in increased LH secretion in rodents.
source: To date, functional studies in rodents have shown that an injection of kisspeptin specifically in to the amygdala results in increased LH secretion, while blocking endogenous amygdala kisspeptin signalling with a kisspeptin antagonist decreases both LH secretion and LH pulsatility (Comninos et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous functional studies.

claim: Blocking endogenous amygdala kisspeptin signalling with a kisspeptin antagonist decreases both LH secretion and LH pulsatility.
source: To date, functional studies in rodents have shown that an injection of kisspeptin specifically in to the amygdala results in increased LH secretion, while blocking endogenous amygdala kisspeptin signalling with a kisspeptin antagonist decreases both LH secretion and LH pulsatility (Comninos et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous functional studies.

claim: NK3R neurons in the MePD may also contain Kiss1r and be activated by both NKB and Kiss1.
source: Thus, we cannot rule out the possibility that NK3R neurons in the MePD also contain Kiss1r and are activated by both NKB and Kiss1.
evidence: This is speculation about potential overlap between the two pathways.

claim: Kiss1MePD and NK3RMePD neurons may be part of the neuronal network linking pheromonal/social cues and gonadotropin release.
source: A reasonable hypothesis is that Kiss1MePD and NK3RMePD neurons are part of the neuronal network linking pheromonal/social cues and gonadotropin release (Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is speculation about the functional relevance of the findings, supported by citation.

claim: Estrogen receptors are expressed in the MePD.
source: Indeed, estrogen receptors are expressed in the MePD (Lymer et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous studies.

claim: The MePD is a central hub for processing sensory inputs such as olfactory signals and integrating these into behavioral and neuroendocrine outputs.
source: and the brain region is a central hub for processing sensory inputs such as olfactory signals and integrating these into behavioral (Rajendren and Moss, 1993; Adekunbi et al., 2018) and neuroendocrine outputs (Pineda et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The kisspeptin-independent, NK3R-dependent pathway may be employed for the generation and/or enhancement of the LH surge and/or female sexual behavior.
source: Specifically, it is compelling to hypothesize that the kisspeptin-independent, NK3R-dependent pathway is employed for the generation and/or enhancement of the LH surge and/or female sexual behavior, for example lordosis, given that this mechanism was absent in male mice, and is exclusively activated in the presence of estrogen, similar to what is observed in the female AVPV/PeN (Smith et al., 2006).
evidence: This is speculation about the functional role of the pathway based on its sex-specific and estrogen-dependent nature.

claim: Exposure to male-soiled bedding enhanced the LH surge in rats and was accompanied by increased Fos expression in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons and various limbic structures, including the MePD.
source: In accordance, recent evidence demonstrated the enhancement of the LH surge in rats exposed to male-soiled bedding, which was accompanied by an increased Fos expression in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons as well as various limbic structures, including the MePD (Watanabe et al., 2017; Hellier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.
